title: Chiquipoli: exact, interval and formal verification of the local maximality of A16, A32, A64, Z32 and Z64
description:
Exact-arithmetic, interval-arithmetic (256-bit) and Lean 4 certification that the Bingane-Audet equilateral small polygons A16, A32 and A64, and the larger-perimeter polygons Z32 and Z64 rebuilt from their description, are strict local maximisers of the perimeter among convex equilateral polygons of diameter at most one, modulo orientation-preserving Euclidean motions. It accompanies the article First-Order Geometry of Equilateral Small Polygons (J. Ayala Hoffmann, T. Ayala Coppola).

What this archive is. Release 1.3.1 contains the certified sources (src/, pipeline/, test/, cases/, lean/), the run records (results/, logs/) and the documentation. The records in results/ were produced by make check-all (13 of 13 stages passed) from Git commit 93e6f9e51d6cf55affa3b8ba7b389270e082b581 with a clean working tree. This release commit differs from that commit only in results/, logs/ and the metadata files CITATION.cff, .zenodo.json and CHANGELOG.md; every source file whose SHA-256 is recorded is byte-identical.

Toolchain. Julia 1.12.6 with IntervalArithmetic.jl 0.22.36 (256-bit BigFloat intervals); Lean 4 toolchain leanprover/lean4:v4.33.0-rc1 with Mathlib revision ae0d973d69b779efa724095bd41793b8cf233831 (pinned in lean/lean-toolchain and lean/lake-manifest.json).

What it does not establish. Global optimality; that Z32 and Z64 are the polygons of Bingane and Audet (they are rebuilt from the description in their Propositions 1 and 2); the fidelity of the transcription of the OPTIGON constructor beyond the checks documented in the article.
